#9786. Setting Up AWS Control Tower? These SCP and Networking Mistakes Can Cost You Hours

Most landing-zone guides stop after "click Set up landing zone". This one keeps going. By the end, you will have a working multi-account AWS environment where every account has one job, the rules are enforced by Service Control Policies, and the network is owned by one account and shared with the others. Each rule is tested from the command line, so you can prove it holds.

Everything here was built in a real organization, including the parts that went wrong: an SCP that broke DNS, an "allow list" SCP that allowed everything, and a RAM share that failed for 40 minutes. The fixes are part of the steps and are collected in the Troubleshooting section.

This is part 1 of a series. Part 2 sets up the Build account (CodeCommit, ECR with cross-account pull, and CodeBuild inside the shared VPC), and part 3 runs the application on ECS in Dev and Production.

Seven accounts, grouped into Organizational Units (OUs), each with one responsibility:

The "must not" rules matter as much as ownership: each one becomes a Deny statement in an SCP, so it holds even for an administrator inside that account.

An AWS account is a hard boundary for IAM permissions, billing, service quotas, and the blast radius of mistakes. When dev, prod, networking, and CI/CD share one account, a developer who needs the dev cluster easily ends up with access to production, and costs can only be split with careful tagging. Separate accounts give you these boundaries for free, and OUs let you apply the same rules to a group of accounts at once: every account you add to the Workloads OU later inherits its guardrails.

The design follows one principle, ownership: for any resource, it should be obvious which account owns it and who is allowed to change it. The network belongs to the Network account, images belong to the Build account, and the running application belongs to the workload account. Images are built once and only pulled by Dev and Production, so Production runs exactly what was tested in Dev.

This article builds only Dev and Production. A Staging account can be added later in exactly the same way.

Control Tower itself is free, but the services it enables are not. Approximate monthly costs in eu-central-1 for this setup:

The NAT gateways are almost all of the bill. If you build this only to learn, follow the Cleanup section when you are done, or delete the NAT gateways between sessions.

Control Tower creates the organization structure, the two shared accounts in the Security OU, an organization-wide CloudTrail trail, and AWS Config in every enrolled account. Everything later in this article builds on it.

Before you start: if IAM Identity Center is already enabled in the management account, Control Tower must be set up in the same Region. Choose the home Region carefully. Changing it later means decommissioning the landing zone.

Sign in to the management account and open AWS Control Tower → Set up landing zone.

On the first page, choose your home Region and Automatic account enrollment. With automatic enrollment, accounts that join the organization later (and accounts you move between OUs) get the Control Tower baseline and controls without manual enrollment.

On the second page, keep the recommended Sandbox OU. It is a place for experiments with fewer restrictions, and we will also use it to test new SCPs before they reach other OUs.

Next, Control Tower asks for the two shared accounts in the Security OU:

The setup takes about 35 minutes. You can follow each step on the landing zone page:

Control Tower created the Security and Sandbox OUs. Create the other three under Root in Control Tower → Organization → Create resources → Create organizational unit: Infrastructure, Deployments, and Workloads. Create them through Control Tower, not the Organizations console, so that they are registered and get the Control Tower controls.

If you expect many workloads, you can nest OUs later, for example Workloads/web and Workloads/ai, and attach different policies to each.

Use Control Tower → Account Factory → Create account for each workload account:

Account Factory provisions accounts one at a time, so creating all four takes a while. When it's done, Control Tower → Organization should show every OU as Registered and every account as Enrolled:

Control Tower configures IAM Identity Center. It creates groups such as AWSControlTowerAdmins, AWSSecurityAuditors, and AWSLogArchiveViewers, and permission sets such as AWSAdministratorAccess, AWSPowerUserAccess, and AWSReadOnlyAccess. In every enrolled account, your user gets AWSAdministratorAccess directly, while the AWSControlTowerAdmins group only gets AWSOrganizationsFullAccess. That direct assignment is how I sign in everywhere in this article:

For a team, don't give everyone administrator access. Create groups by role and assign each group only to the accounts it needs:

In the console: IAM Identity Center → Groups → Create group, then AWS accounts → select the accounts → Assign users or groups → choose the group and the permission set. The same assignment from the CLI:

For the command line, add one profile per account to ~/.aws/config, then sign in once with aws sso login --sso-session lz. One sign-in covers all profiles:

Tip: use the role name that you actually see in the access portal. In my organization the management account has AdministratorAccess while member accounts have AWSAdministratorAccess. A wrong role name fails with "ForbiddenException: No access".

Also check that no AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID or AWS_SESSION_TOKEN environment variables are set in your shell. The CLI uses them whenever a command has no --profile, so a single forgotten flag silently runs that command against a completely different account. I had exactly this situation, with keys for an unrelated organization in my shell.

Service Control Policies (SCPs) are guardrails in AWS Organizations. They define the maximum permissions available to IAM users and roles in the accounts of an OU, regardless of what their IAM policies allow.

We use them to enforce the Region, to block dangerous actions (leaving the organization, disabling security services), to enforce ownership (only the Network account builds connectivity), and to remove risky shortcuts (root user, long-lived access keys). SCPs say "what's possible", IAM policies say "who can do it".

We don't attach our policies to the Security OU. Control Tower manages the Audit and Log Archive accounts and already protects them with its own guardrails (the aws-guardrails-* policies you can see in the list).

Every Deny statement below has an exception for the AWSControlTowerExecution role and the stacksets-exec-* roles. Control Tower uses these roles to manage the accounts, and blocking them would break enrollment and drift repair.

Go to AWS Organizations → Policies → Service control policies → Create policy, and name it BaselineGuardrails :

The Network account owns connectivity. FullAWSAccess already allows that, so we only add what it must not do: run applications or CI/CD.

The Build account owns pipelines and container images. It must not create its own network connectivity (Transit Gateway, peering, VPN, Direct Connect) and must not run application services or databases.

Dev and Production run the application. They may attach their VPC to a Transit Gateway shared by the Network account, but cannot build their own connectivity, create ECR repositories, push images, or create pipelines. Images are built once in the Build account and only pulled here.

Select the policy → Actions → Attach policy, and choose the OU:

Leave FullAWSAccess attached. Our policies only take permissions away from it.

The final picture for the Workloads OU should be: FullAWSAccess, the Control Tower aws-guardrails-* policy, BaselineGuardrails, and WorkloadsECSPolicy:

Always test SCPs right after attaching them. EC2 supports --dry-run, which checks permissions without creating anything:

The error message names the exact SCP that denied the request, which makes troubleshooting much easier. Section 7 has a script that tests all guardrails at once.

Tip: before attaching a new SCP to a production OU, attach it to the Sandbox OU or a test account first. A wrong Deny statement affects every account in the OU immediately.

With the guardrails in place, we can build the network. The Network account owns all VPCs, subnets, route tables, NAT gateways, and internet gateways. Dev, Production, and Build don't create VPCs. They receive subnets from the Network account through AWS Resource Access Manager (RAM).

One shared VPC for everyone would put Dev and Production on the same network. Instead, each environment gets its own VPC, shared only with its own account, and we don't need a Transit Gateway yet.

Before creating anything, plan the IP ranges. VPCs that may need to be connected later (with Transit Gateway or peering) must not overlap. Control Tower created a VPC in every account with the same 172.31.0.0/16 range, and these VPCs can never be connected to each other.

We reserve a /16 range for each environment:

Each environment VPC uses two Availability Zones and three subnet tiers:

The app subnets are larger (/20, about 4,000 addresses) because every ECS task on Fargate gets its own IP address. Production uses the same layout with 10.20.x.x. The build VPC needs only two public and two private subnets (10.30.0.0/24, 10.30.1.0/24, 10.30.16.0/20, 10.30.32.0/20).

Control Tower's Account Factory created an empty VPC named aws-controltower-VPC in every new account. We don't need them, so delete them in the Network, Build, Dev, and Production accounts (VPC → Your VPCs → select aws-controltower-VPC → Actions → Delete VPC).

To prevent Control Tower from creating these VPCs in future accounts, go to Control Tower → Account Factory → Network configuration → Edit, and set the maximum number of private subnets to 0.

Sign in to the Network account, open VPC → Create VPC, and choose VPC and more. This wizard creates the VPC, subnets, route tables, internet gateway, NAT gateway, and VPC endpoints in one step.

Expand Customize subnets CIDR blocks and enter the CIDRs from the table above. The wizard's defaults would give the public subnets /20 ranges, which wastes addresses we want to keep for ECS tasks.

ECS tasks in private subnets need outbound access to pull container images, send logs, and call external APIs. This is the job of the NAT gateway. The wizard offers three options:

We make a different choice per environment:

For prod, choose Regional instead of Zonal. There is no AZ selection for a regional NAT gateway, because AWS manages its availability across zones:

Choose S3 Gateway. Gateway endpoints are free. Amazon ECR stores image layers in S3, so most of the traffic when ECS pulls an image goes through the endpoint instead of the NAT gateway, which reduces NAT data processing costs.

We don't create interface endpoints (ECR, CloudWatch Logs, STS) yet. At about $0.01 per hour per AZ each, five of them in two AZs cost more than the NAT gateway they would replace.

Keep DNS hostnames and DNS resolution enabled.

Before creating the VPC, check the Preview panel on the right. It shows every resource the wizard will create. You should see six subnets, one internet gateway, one NAT gateway, and private route tables with a 0.0.0.0/0 route to the NAT gateway.

Click Create VPC. Creating the NAT gateway takes a minute or two.

Open the VPC and look at the Resource map tab. It shows the whole design on one screen: six subnets in two AZs, the public route table pointing to the internet gateway, and the private route tables pointing to the NAT gateway and the S3 endpoint.

Repeat the same steps for prod (10.20.0.0/16, Regional NAT gateway) and build (10.30.0.0/16, 2 public and 2 private subnets, Zonal NAT gateway in 1 AZ).

First, allow RAM to share resources within the organization. In the management account, open Resource Access Manager → Settings and enable Enable sharing with AWS Organizations. Without this setting, resources can only be shared through invitations.

Now, in the Network account, open Resource Access Manager → Resource shares → Create resource share:

When I created the first share, it failed with this error, even though organization sharing was enabled a few minutes earlier:

The message suggests waiting for onboarding to finish, but mine still failed after 40 minutes, from every account. The real hint came from the CLI: sharing with the organization as principal returned UnknownResourceException: Organization o-xxxxxxxx. RAM had never imported the organization, even though the Organizations console listed RAM as a trusted service.

The fix was to reset RAM trusted access from the management account:

Run this only before you have any resource shares. Disabling trusted access affects existing organization-based shares. After the reset, sharing worked within a minute.

Before that, I ruled out our own SCP by detaching BaselineGuardrails from the Infrastructure OU for a minute. A good habit in a governed account: rule out your own SCPs first. The error message names the denying SCP, as in this example where the region lock blocks CloudTrail in us-east-1:

Sign in to the Dev account and open VPC → Subnets. The shared subnets appear with the Network account as the owner.

Guardrails are easy to get subtly wrong, so I keep a script that checks the important rules in one run. It only uses read-only calls and EC2 --dry-run, so it never creates anything:

The "allow" checks matter too: a guardrail that blocks too much is also a bug, like my first region lock that broke Route 53. Run the script after every SCP change.

Every problem I hit while building this part, in one place:

If you built this only to learn, delete it in this order. Participants must remove their resources from shared subnets before the owner can delete them.

Dev, Production, and Build accounts: delete anything you launched into the shared subnets, including security groups.

Network account: delete the three RAM shares. Then delete the NAT gateways and release their Elastic IP addresses (this stops most of the cost), and delete the three VPCs.

Management account: detach and delete the four custom SCPs. To remove everything, decommission the landing zone in Control Tower, then close the member accounts. Closed accounts stay suspended for 90 days.

We now have a landing zone where every account has one clear job, and the boundaries are enforced rather than just documented:

Benchmarking AWS Amplify, Lambda, Web Functions, and ECS for Next.js

#9785. Sellfy Review 2022: How Good Is This Ecommerce Platform?

Are you searching for an ecomerce platform to help you build an online store and sell products?

In this Sellfy review, we'll talk about how this eCommerce platform can let you sell digital products while keeping full control of your marketing.

And the best part? Starting your business can be done in just five minutes.

Let us then talk about the Sellfy platform and all the benefits it can bring to your business.

Sellfy is an eCommerce solution that allows digital content creators, including writers, illustrators, designers, musicians, and filmmakers, to sell their products online. Sellfy provides a customizable storefront where users can display their digital products and embed "Buy Now" buttons on their website or blog. Sellfy product pages enable users to showcase their products from different angles with multiple images and previews from Soundcloud, Vimeo, and YouTube. Files of up to 2GB can be uploaded to Sellfy, and the company offers unlimited bandwidth and secure file storage. Users can also embed their entire store or individual project widgets in their site, with the ability to preview how widgets will appear before they are displayed.

Sellfy is a powerful e-commerce platform that helps you personalize your online storefront. You can add your logo, change colors, revise navigation, and edit the layout of your store. Sellfy also allows you to create a full shopping cart so customers can purchase multiple items. And Sellfy gives you the ability to set your language or let customers see a translated version of your store based on their location.

Sellfy gives you the option to host your store directly on its platform, add a custom domain to your store, and use it as an embedded storefront on your website. Sellfy also optimizes its store offerings for mobile devices, allowing for a seamless checkout experience.

Sellfy allows creators to host all their products and sell all of their digital products on one platform. Sellfy also does not place storage limits on your store but recommends that files be no larger than 5GB. Creators can sell both standard and subscription-based products in any file format that is supported by the online marketplace. Customers can purchase products instantly after making a purchase – there is no waiting period.

You can organize your store by creating your product categories, sorting by any characteristic you choose. Your title, description, and the image will be included on each product page. In this way, customers can immediately evaluate all of your products. You can offer different pricing options for all of your products, including "pay what you want," in which the price is entirely up to the customer. This option allows you to give customers control over the cost of individual items (without a minimum price) or to set pricing minimums—a good option if you're in a competitive market or when you have higher-end products. You can also offer set prices per product as well as free products to help build your store's popularity.

Sellfy is ideal for selling digital content, such as ebooks. But it does not allow you to copyrighted material (that you don't have rights to distribute).

Sellfy offers several ways to share your store, enabling you to promote your business on different platforms. Sellfy lets you integrate it with your existing website using "buy now" buttons, embed your entire storefront, or embed certain products so you can reach more people. Sellfy also enables you to connect with your Facebook page and YouTube channel, maximizing your visibility.

Sellfy is a simple online platform that allows customers to buy your products directly through your store. Sellfy has two payment processing options: PayPal and Stripe. You will receive instant payments with both of these processors, and your customer data is protected by Sellfy's secure (PCI-compliant) payment security measures. In addition to payment security, Sellfy provides anti-fraud tools to help protect your products including PDF stamping, unique download links, and limited download attempts.

To expand functionality and make your e-commerce store run more efficiently, Sellfy offers several integrations. Google Analytics and Webhooks, as well as integrations with Patreon and Facebook Live Chat, are just a few of the options available. Sellfy allows you to connect to Zapier, which gives you access to hundreds of third-party apps, including tools like Mailchimp, Trello, Salesforce, and more.

Sellfy has its benefits and downsides, but fortunately, the pros outweigh the cons.

In this article, we have taken a look at some of the biggest benefits associated with using sellfy for eCommerce. Once you compare these benefits to what you get with other platforms such as Shopify, you should find that it is worth your time to consider sellfy for your business. #9784. Nurses, store staff and technicians: what 563,000 open Workday jobs say about who is hiring

Tech job data usually comes from Greenhouse, Lever and Ashby, the systems startups use. But most American jobs are posted somewhere else: on Workday, the career site behind hospitals, retailers, banks, universities and manufacturers. Walmart, Bank of America, Boeing, Medtronic, Johnson & Johnson, PwC, CVS Health and Lowe's all run their hiring on *.myworkdayjobs.com.

We read about 3,300 Workday career sites every night. The November 18, 2026 build holds 563,302 open jobs. Here is what they look like.

Registered nurses alone outnumber software engineers more than two to one. On Greenhouse it is the other way round: 7,341 software engineer jobs against 1,675 nurse jobs.

Only 2.6% of Workday jobs are marked remote, against 13.9% on Greenhouse and 29.9% on Ashby. Workday's employers hire people to be in a hospital, a store, a plant or a campus.

About half of the jobs (51%) are in the US, then Canada (2.6%), India (2.5%), the UK (1.5%), Germany, Singapore and China. For about 30% the listing names only a campus or hospital ("Main Campus", "Strong Memorial Hospital") or "3 Locations", so the country is not stated in the list itself.

Among US jobs with a state, the most are in Texas (about 18,800), California (13,200), New York (9,300), Florida (9,000), Pennsylvania (8,300), Massachusetts (7,400) and Virginia (6,700).

Workday lists show "Posted Today", "Posted 3 Days Ago" and so on for a job's first 30 days, then only "Posted 30+ Days Ago". Of the jobs with a date in the list, 43% were posted in the last 7 days: big employers post and repost all the time. For older jobs you need the job's own page, which has the exact startDate.

Each Workday site answers a public JSON endpoint (/wday/cxs///jobs); we explained it, with its quirks, in an earlier post. The hard part is the list of sites: there is no directory, and each tenant has its own host and site name.

To search all of them at once, use Workday Jobs API on Apify. It searches our nightly copy of every site in seconds: a job title and a location in, matching jobs out, newest first, with the description and apply link.

The price is $0.01 per search plus $0.002 per job. For every job of a few chosen companies, read live, there is Workday Jobs Scraper; for Workday together with 23,000 other career sites, Jobs Database API. Which companies are hiring for a role right now, without code: Companies Hiring Now.

One night's crawl of the public job lists; very large sites are read up to a limit of a few thousand newest jobs, so the counts for the biggest employers are lower bounds. Titles are matched by keywords; a job counts once, in the first row it matches. Remote means the employer marked it remote or the location says so.

#9782. What is high-extraction flour, exactly?  : A baker’s guide to our new T85 Baker's Reserve Bread Flour.

High-extraction flour is a technical term that often prompts a lot of confusion from those unfamiliar with it. But with the debut of our new high-extraction flour, known as Baker’s Reserve Bread Flour, we’re breaking down just what it is and why it's a great choice for avid bread makers.

The extraction rate of a flour refers to how much of the original grain — the bran, germ, and endosperm — ends up in the final flour. A high-extraction flour typically has an extraction rate of about 80% to 90%, meaning some of the bran and germ have been sifted out, but it still retains much of the original grain. Our Baker’s Reserve Bread Flour is a T85 flour, meaning its extraction rate is 85%.

To put that in perspective, whole wheat flour has an extraction rate of 100%; it retains the entirety of the grain, including the bran, germ, and endosperm.

High-extraction flour falls between white and whole wheat flour. It’s lighter and less coarse than whole wheat flour because some of the bran has been sifted out, but it still retains more flavor, nutrients, and color than white flour, since it retains much of the original grain.

High-extraction flour is popular for artisan bread baking because it offers a balance of nutrition and good gluten development. It’s great for rustic loaves, baguettes, and pizza dough, and particularly well-suited for sourdough baking because it strikes a balance between flavor, nutrition, fermentation, and dough strength.

You can substitute our Baker’s Reserve Bread Flour 1:1 for bread flour (by weight or volume) in artisanal bread recipes; it can also be used 1:1 to replace the total flour in recipes that call for a combination of all-purpose and whole wheat flour. If you're subbing Baker’s Reserve Bread Flour for all-purpose flour in a bread recipe, you may find you need to add slightly more liquid to the recipe.

Bread bakers love high-extraction flour for artisan bread and sourdough because it offers the flavor and nutrition of whole grain flour; the stronger gluten development and more open crumb you get from white flour; and better fermentation from the minerals present in the bran and germ, which feed the wild yeast and lactic acid bacteria in sourdough starter, promoting more active fermentation.

If you want a loaf of bread that’s more flavorful and nutritious than bread made with exclusively white flour, but that still rises high and has an open crumb, high-extraction flour is a great choice.

Yes — in fact, it’s a great choice for feeding starter because of the sourdough-friendly minerals present in the flour, which boost activity in your starter.

Yes! T85 is a French specification that refers to the extraction rate (85%) of the flour. Our Baker’s Reserve Bread Flour is a T85 flour, meaning the extraction rate is 85%. If you have a recipe that calls for T85, this flour is the perfect choice.

#9779. Cloudflare AI Crawl Control WAF Rules: Fix Rule Conflicts

Posted on Nov 21 • Originally published at mecanik.dev

Cloudflare AI Crawl Control WAF rules need to be understood as part of a request path, not as independent switches. A crawler can be blocked by another control even when its Crawl Control setting looks permissive. Diagnosing that mismatch requires evidence of the rule that acted on the request.

Define the intended crawler and path policy, then trace the relevant WAF, bot and origin decisions in their documented order. Test both permitted and blocked cases and retain the effective rule evidence. Change the narrow conflicting condition rather than removing broad protections merely to make a crawler request succeed.

Imagine a publisher that wants ordinary search discovery while restricting selected AI crawlers. The dashboard policy looks correct, but an earlier custom rule blocks the request before the intended later behaviour can occur. Alternatively, an origin application may deny a request that Cloudflare allowed through.

This guide addresses implementation and diagnosis. For the earlier commercial decision, see our AI crawler business guide. It does not promise improved rankings, guaranteed crawler identification or income from content access.

Write the intended behaviour in plain language before editing rules. Identify the crawler category, hostname, path and purpose. “Block unwanted scraping” is too vague to prove that an important search route remains available.

Cloudflare's Crawl Control getting-started guide describes visibility and crawler controls. Review the detection available on the actual plan and avoid treating a user-agent string as conclusive proof of who sent a request.

Keep policy ownership explicit. The person responsible for search visibility and the person responsible for security should agree the intended result before a diagnostic change becomes a permanent exception.

Cloudflare's Crawl Control and WAF documentation explains that AI crawler blocking uses WAF custom rules and that pay-per-crawl processing takes place later. The bot interaction guide places the relevant bot controls between those stages.

A later setting cannot help a request that an earlier applicable control has already blocked. That is the core reason apparently contradictory settings can coexist without producing the result the publisher expects.

Do not generalize this simplified relationship into a complete ordering of every Cloudflare security product. Inspect the relevant current documentation and actual request evidence for the features enabled on the zone.

For the publisher, draw the path through the controls involved in the reported failure. Include the origin after Cloudflare where relevant. An origin refusal should not be “fixed” by weakening an unrelated edge rule.

Proposed design. Trace the effective request path. View full-size diagram

Start with a concrete URL, observation time, response and intended outcome. Obtain the relevant event or request evidence available to the account. A report that “the crawler is blocked” without a path or time is difficult to reproduce.

Identify which layer produced the response. Check whether a security rule matched, a bot setting acted or the request reached the origin. A generic error page or a failed automated probe is a clue, not the final diagnosis.

Use a normal GET when verifying whether public content resolves. A failed HEAD request can reflect method handling rather than a broken page. This repository's link history already shows why changing working content on a HEAD-only result is unsafe.

Do not claim that a manual request with a copied crawler user agent proves the real crawler is allowed. It can test a rule condition, but it does not reproduce all classification and identity signals of the actual service.

Once the evidence identifies the conflict, change the smallest policy condition that achieves the intended behaviour. Keep unrelated private routes and security controls under their existing requirements.

For a path-specific exception, verify the hostname and path boundaries deliberately. A broad prefix can include administrative or customer content that the publisher did not intend to expose. Test neighbouring paths as well as the example that triggered the report.

Record the previous configuration and rollback procedure. A diagnostic experiment should have an explicit end condition so a temporary broad exception does not become an undocumented permanent policy.

Proposed design. Trace the effective request path. View full-size diagram

Robots directives communicate a site's requested crawling behaviour. Enforcement decisions belong to the controls actually serving the request. A crawler's presence or absence in a robots file does not prove that the configured WAF and bot rules produce the intended access result.

Review both together. A public policy that says one thing while request enforcement does another confuses the publisher, crawlers and anyone diagnosing traffic. Keep the documented intention aligned with the tested behaviour.

Where detection relies on self-identification, make that limitation explicit in the operational report. Do not describe the setting as a guarantee that all AI-originated access has been identified and stopped.

Avoid importing historical monetization claims into this configuration work. If charging is part of the brief, verify current account eligibility and product status separately. Successful crawler access does not establish a payment agreement or a revenue outcome.

Build a small regression matrix from the agreed policy. The publisher needs evidence that the intended crawler path works and that the restriction still acts on the cases it should control.

Record what each test actually establishes. Synthetic requests are useful for condition testing; actual crawler events provide different evidence. Keep the distinction in the report rather than presenting a spoofed user-agent test as verification of an external service's behaviour.

Repeat relevant tests after another rule or bot-setting change. A configuration that is correct today can be affected by a future exception higher in the path. The runbook should tell the next engineer where to look first.

The cost depends on the enabled controls, number of hostnames, path structure, available evidence and whether the origin has its own access logic. A simple dashboard switch is a smaller task than reconciling several overlapping policies.

Request a GBP proposal with the affected URLs, intended crawler categories and current symptoms. Include the rule inventory, evidence review, scoped correction, regression matrix and rollback. Avoid a quote that promises an SEO outcome from a security-setting change.

The handover should identify the effective conditions, owner and review triggers for each exception. It should also explain the limits of the tests performed and any external crawler behaviour that remains unverified.

We can review the request path through our website security service. Send the affected URLs and observed responses with the access policy you want to enforce. That gives the investigation a concrete target while preserving a clear record of why each rule exists.

Why can a crawler remain blocked after we allow it in Crawl Control? Another applicable control may act earlier, or the origin may reject the request after it passes Cloudflare. Trace a specific request and identify the effective rule or response source rather than assuming the visible crawler setting is the only decision.

Does a copied crawler user agent prove the real crawler can access the site? No. It can help test a condition based on that header, but it does not reproduce every identity or classification signal. Distinguish synthetic rule tests from evidence of actual crawler requests.

Should we disable the WAF to diagnose the problem? Use request evidence and narrow tests first. A broad removal changes behaviour for unrelated traffic and may hide the real conflict. Identify the condition responsible and make a scoped, reversible correction.

Is robots.txt the same as an enforced block? No. Directives express requested crawling behaviour; the serving controls determine whether a request is allowed. Review directives and enforcement together and verify that their intended policy agrees.

Does allowing an AI crawler improve rankings? This configuration work does not establish a ranking outcome. Its purpose is to make the intended request policy work and to document its limits. Search performance needs separate evidence and should not be promised from a rule change.

What should a rule-conflict assessment include? Include the intended policy, affected URLs, request evidence, relevant control order, scoped changes and regression tests. Provide rollback instructions and identify which observations come from synthetic tests versus actual crawler activity.

How should we estimate the work? Describe the hostnames, paths, enabled controls, origin behaviour and symptoms. Request a scoped GBP proposal for diagnosis, correction, verification and handover. The amount of overlap between policies matters more than the number of dashboard switches.

#9777. ProWritingAid VS Grammarly: Which Grammar Checker is Better in (2022) ?

Grammarly is a tool that checks for grammatical errors, spelling, and punctuation.it gives you comprehensive feedback on your writing. You can use this tool to proofread and edit articles, blog posts, emails, etc.

Grammarly also detects all types of mistakes, including sentence structure issues and misused words. It also gives you suggestions on style changes, punctuation, spelling, and grammar all are in real-time. The free version covers the basics like identifying grammar and spelling mistakes

whereas the Premium version offers a lot more functionality, it detects plagiarism in your content, suggests word choice, or adds fluency to it.

ProWritingAid is a style and grammar checker for content creators and writers. It helps to optimize word choice, punctuation errors, and common grammar mistakes, providing detailed reports to help you improve your writing.

ProWritingAid can be used as an add-on to WordPress, Gmail, and Google Docs. The software also offers helpful articles, videos, quizzes, and explanations to help improve your writing.

Here are some key features of ProWriting Aid:

Grammarly and ProWritingAid are well-known grammar-checking software. However, if you're like most people who can't decide which to use, here are some different points that may be helpful in your decision.

As both writing assistants are great in their own way, you need to choose the one that suits you best.

Both ProWritingAid and Grammarly are awesome writing tools, without a doubt. but as per my experience, Grammarly is a winner here because Grammarly helps you to review and edit your content. Grammarly highlights all the mistakes in your writing within seconds of copying and pasting the content into Grammarly’s editor or using the software’s native feature in other text editors.

Not only does it identify tiny grammatical and spelling errors, it tells you when you overlook punctuations where they are needed. And, beyond its plagiarism-checking capabilities, Grammarly helps you proofread your content. Even better, the software offers a free plan that gives you access to some of its features.

Sounds like you're biased for Grammarly. Not really that informative if you're already leaning towards one to begin with. Still, it was an interesting read. Tell me, do you use Grammarly with your day-to-day writing/blogging?

I use the paid versions of both Grammarly and Pro Writing Aid. Both of them have issues:- Grammarly IS more focused on nonfiction than fiction. If you're writing fiction, you may find Grammarly's insistence on "Conciseness" annoying. They seem to want to take the soul out of your writing, which is fine for a corporate report or technical manual, but not for your Great American Novel.- Grammarly pushes features on users that are not ready for prime time. It doesn't matter that you never agreed to be a beta tester for them; you get to do it anyway.- Pro Writing Aid actually counts the occurrences of words in your document and tells you when a word has been overused compared to published literature. Grammarly, on the other hand, seems hell-bent to remove certain words that it has deemed overused from the language, whether or not they're actually overused in your document.- Grammarly's Clarity function is simply horrible. It mangles sentences and changes their meaning. Sometimes the result of its suggestion is unintelligible garbage.- Grammarly allows you to turn off some checks, but not all of them. Unfortunately, the ones you cannot turn off are some of the most irritating (such as that horrible "Clarity"). On the other hand, Pro Writing Aid lets you choose which checks you use.- Pro Writing Aid has a mediocre command of American English (it's a British product). The app insists on rules of grammar and spelling that are outright wrong, per Merriam-Webster, the Chicago Manual of Style, and modern usage as shown by Google Books Ngram. At one point, Pro Writing Aid insisted that American English did not include the words "holiday" and "autumn," that "vacation" and "fall" must be used instead.- Pro Writing Aid's rules for commas are 100 percent consistent with the way I learned them in high school--50 years ago! They do not reflect modern usage. Grammarly is much better at this.- Pro Writing Aid seems to waste their limited resources on tweaking their UI. Their UI most definitely could use improvement, but these changes are not great improvements; they only serve to confuse users. Their resources would be better spent fixing the many functional problems in their app.- Some of Pro Writing Aid's checks are completely useless, as they do not take context into consideration. For example, an ordinary word would not be capitalized as part of a narrative, but would be as part of a title (for example, "professor." But if you capitalize correctly for context, Pro Writing Aid dings you for "Inconsistent capitalization." Similar issues exist with hyphenation consistency check.Each of these applications has its strengths as well as considerable weaknesses. I will say that both of them are light-years better than the execrable grammar checker in Microsoft Word, but that's damning with faint praise.

What do jobs, school, sports practices, and commuting have in common? They all prevent us from baking as much or as often as we’d like. But when we do get the chance, we want a slam-dunk recipe — or 12. Here’s a dozen of the favorite fall recipes we’ll be making this month: from pumpkin cake bars to spooky fudge brownies to a crowd-pleasing vegetarian quiche.

It’s the Great Pumpkin, Charlie Brown! Only this version comes in cake form. The decoration is deceptively easy: Stack two small Bundts, frost the entire thing, and add a chocolate-dipped ice cream cone for the stem.

Get the recipe: The Great Pumpkin Bundt Cake

To make this recipe, you’ll need: Golden Wheat Flour and Pumpkin Pie Spice

If you like this recipe, you may also like: Pumpkin Espresso Bundt Cake, Gluten-Free Pumpkin Cake

These bite-sized pies are a charming addition to any occasion. The boiled cider and spices in the filling ensure a full depth of apple flavor for maximum fall vibes. If you're tight on time, swap the lattice treatment for a buttery crumb topping instead.

To make this recipe, you’ll need: Boiled Cider and Apple Pie Spice

If you like this recipe, you may also like: Apple Pie Bars, Tiny Apple Tarts for Two

Step aside, soup: Butternut squash truly shines in this autumnal quiche. Caramelized onions finished with balsamic vinegar and fresh baby spinach round out the filling, while our Classic Single Pie Crust recipe ensures a tender, golden crust. Elevate the edges with the pie crust decorating technique of your choice.

Ready to test the theory that only white flour can make rolls light and fluffy? A bit of bread flour and vital wheat gluten give these whole wheat rolls a lofty rise, while the milk, butter, and honey create a plush crumb that stays soft for days. Add a salted honey butter wash to the tops of a freshly baked batch, and you may not have any leftover.

To make this recipe, you’ll need: Golden Wheat Flour and Bread Flour

If you like this recipe, you may also like: Whole Grain Dinner Rolls, Soft White Dinner Rolls

"Tassie" means "small cup" in Scottish, and these dainty pecan pies pack a nutty punch. The cream cheese pastry crust is cut into rounds and placed in a mini muffin pan before the pecan pie filling is spooned into each well. With only 30 minutes of hands-on time, these two dozen tassies come together quickly on a crisp fall afternoon.

To make this recipe, you’ll need: Mini Muffin Pan

If you like this recipe, you may also like: Easy Pecan Pie Bars, Old-Fashioned Pecan Pie

Need a spooky treat, stat? You can transform a plain batch of brownies into a Halloween-themed dessert in a pinch. A simple piping technique creates a spider web effect and adds a touch of rich tang to chocolatey brownies.

'Tis the season for hand pies to be mummified! A shortening-based pie crust helps the lattice strips stay together, while jam or pie filling allows for customizable flavors. Pop on a few sugar eyes, and you'll be sure to have treats instead of tricks.

With a luxuriously creamy maple filling and a buttery pecan crust, this cheesecake balances richness with subtle flavors. Meanwhile, the candied pecan garnish adds visual interest and a complementary crunch. Be sure to leave time for an overnight chill and keep your cheesecake from cracking with these tips. (Find more seasonal maple recipes in our Fall Flavor Edit.)

#9770. Quarantine the tool result: a code-level defence for injected agent output

Posted on Nov 21 • Originally published at loopandretry.github.io

Originally published on Loop & Retry — field notes on building LLM agents that survive production.

Most advice on indirect prompt injection stops at "treat tool output as untrusted." That's right, and tool output is untrusted input makes the data-flow argument for it. How indirect prompt injection actually happens walks the pipeline from placement to execution. Neither tells you what to type into your agent loop on Monday morning.

This post is that. It assumes the model will sometimes follow an injected instruction, because it will, and asks a different question: what does the code around the model do so that a followed injection can't hurt much? Three pieces: a quarantine envelope, taint-driven capability scoping, and a replay harness.

The usual agent loop appends the raw tool string to the conversation. From that moment the attacker's text sits in the same channel as your instructions, with nothing marking where it came from.

Make provenance a type, not a convention:

Every tool wrapper returns a ToolResult, never a bare string, and the loop refuses to append anything else. The system prompt then says, once, that content inside tool_result is data to be summarised or extracted from, and never instructions to follow.

Be honest about what this buys. It does not make injection impossible; a model can still be talked past a delimiter. What it gives you is (a) a reliable signal for the rest of your code, which is the part you actually control, and (b) a measurable improvement in how often the model resists, which you can test (pattern 3). The envelope is the hook the next two patterns hang on.

The point of an injection is almost never to make the model say something. It's to make the model do something: send the email, call the webhook, write the file. So don't gate on what the model says it intends; gate on what it is allowed to do given what it has read.

Track a taint bit on the session. Once any UNTRUSTED result enters context, the session is tainted, and every tool is checked against a capability policy:

Three details that are easy to get wrong:

When one task needs both, use two model calls with a narrow channel between them. A reader sees the untrusted document and has no tools with side effects. It returns a constrained structure. A separate actor has the powerful tools and never sees the raw text, only the validated structure.

The attacker still controls one_line, so it can carry a short injected string; the schema's job is to make that channel as small and as boring as possible. The enums and integers are the safe fields. Free text is the leak, so keep it short, don't feed it to a privileged prompt as instructions, and prefer fields the actor can branch on without reading. This is the same instinct as validating tool output: a schema check at the boundary is cheap, and skipping it is where the compounding cost comes from. Here the check just happens to be a security control too.

The first two patterns are claims. Claims about security that nobody tests rot quietly: someone adds a tool, labels it READ, and it turns out to POST. So test the whole loop with a corpus of payloads and a canary.

The test is simple. Plant a payload in a fixture the agent will legitimately read. The payload tries to make the agent call a tool, with a canary token as the argument. Run the agent. Assert the canary never reaches a side-effecting tool.

Be clear about the boundary, so you don't oversell it to yourself.

Taint-gating protects against actions. It does nothing about an injection that corrupts the answer: a poisoned page that makes the agent confidently summarise falsehoods is still a failure, one that needs provenance in the output and a human who checks sources. It also doesn't help where your tools aren't labelled; an unlabelled tool should default to the most restrictive capability, not the least, so the check fails closed.

And the human-approval escape hatch is itself an attack surface. If the approval prompt shows the model's description of what it's about to do, the attacker wrote that description. Show the literal tool name and arguments, rendered by your code.

None of this makes the model trustworthy. It makes the model's trustworthiness stop being the thing your security depends on, which is the only version of this problem you get to win.

#9769. What is Blockchain: Everything You Need to Know (2022)

Imagine a world in which you can do transactions and many other things without having to give your personal information. A world in which you don’t need to rely on banks or governments anymore. Sounds amazing, right? That’s exactly what blockchain technology allows us to do.

It’s like your computer’s hard drive. blockchain is a technology that lets you store data in digital blocks, which are connected together like links in a chain.

Blockchain technology was originally invented in 1991 by two mathematicians, Stuart Haber and W. Scot Stornetta. They first proposed the system to ensure that timestamps could not be tampered with.

A few years later, in 1998, software developer Nick Szabo proposed using a similar kind of technology to secure a digital payments system he called “Bit Gold.” However, this innovation was not adopted until Satoshi Nakamoto claimed to have invented the first Blockchain and Bitcoin.

A blockchain is a distributed database shared between the nodes of a computer network. It saves information in digital format. Many people first heard of blockchain technology when they started to look up information about bitcoin.

Blockchain is used in cryptocurrency systems to ensure secure, decentralized records of transactions.

Blockchain allowed people to guarantee the fidelity and security of a record of data without the need for a third party to ensure accuracy.

To understand how a blockchain works, Consider these basic steps:

Let’s get to know more about the blockchain.

Blockchain records digital information and distributes it across the network without changing it. The information is distributed among many users and stored in an immutable, permanent ledger that can't be changed or destroyed. That's why blockchain is also called "Distributed Ledger Technology" or DLT.

And that’s the beauty of it! The process may seem complicated, but it’s done in minutes with modern technology. And because technology is advancing rapidly, I expect things to move even more quickly than ever.

Even though blockchain is integral to cryptocurrency, it has other applications. For example, blockchain can be used for storing reliable data about transactions. Many people confuse blockchain with cryptocurrencies like bitcoin and ethereum.

Blockchain already being adopted by some big-name companies, such as Walmart, AIG, Siemens, Pfizer, and Unilever. For example, IBM's Food Trust uses blockchain to track food's journey before reaching its final destination.

Although some of you may consider this practice excessive, food suppliers and manufacturers adhere to the policy of tracing their products because bacteria such as E. coli and Salmonella have been found in packaged foods. In addition, there have been isolated cases where dangerous allergens such as peanuts have accidentally been introduced into certain products.

Tracing and identifying the sources of an outbreak is a challenging task that can take months or years. Thanks to the Blockchain, however, companies now know exactly where their food has been—so they can trace its location and prevent future outbreaks.

Blockchain technology allows systems to react much faster in the event of a hazard. It also has many other uses in the modern world.

Blockchain technology is safe, even if it’s public. People can access the technology using an internet connection.

Have you ever been in a situation where you had all your data stored at one place and that one secure place got compromised? Wouldn't it be great if there was a way to prevent your data from leaking out even when the security of your storage systems is compromised?

Blockchain technology provides a way of avoiding this situation by using multiple computers at different locations to store information about transactions. If one computer experiences problems with a transaction, it will not affect the other nodes.

Instead, other nodes will use the correct information to cross-reference your incorrect node. This is called “Decentralization,” meaning all the information is stored in multiple places.

Blockchain guarantees your data's authenticity—not just its accuracy, but also its irreversibility. It can also be used to store data that are difficult to register, like legal contracts, state identifications, or a company's product inventory.

Blockchain has many advantages and disadvantages.

I’ll answer the most frequently asked questions about blockchain in this section.

Blockchain is not a cryptocurrency but a technology that makes cryptocurrencies possible. It's a digital ledger that records every transaction seamlessly.

Yes, blockchain can be theoretically hacked, but it is a complicated task to be achieved. A network of users constantly reviews it, which makes hacking the blockchain difficult.

Coinbase Global is currently the biggest blockchain company in the world. The company runs a commendable infrastructure, services, and technology for the digital currency economy.

Blockchain is a decentralized technology. It’s a chain of distributed ledgers connected with nodes. Each node can be any electronic device. Thus, one owns blockhain.

Bitcoin is a cryptocurrency, which is powered by Blockchain technology while Blockchain is a distributed ledger of cryptocurrency

Generally a database is a collection of data which can be stored and organized using a database management system. The people who have access to the database can view or edit the information stored there. The client-server network architecture is used to implement databases. whereas a blockchain is a growing list of records, called blocks, stored in a distributed system. Each block contains a cryptographic hash of the previous block, timestamp and transaction information. Modification of data is not allowed due to the design of the blockchain. The technology allows decentralized control and eliminates risks of data modification by other parties.

Blockchain has a wide spectrum of applications and, over the next 5-10 years, we will likely see it being integrated into all sorts of industries. From finance to healthcare, blockchain could revolutionize the way we store and share data. Although there is some hesitation to adopt blockchain systems right now, that won't be the case in 2022-2023 (and even less so in 2026). Once people become more comfortable with the technology and understand how it can work for them, owners, CEOs and entrepreneurs alike will be quick to leverage blockchain technology for their own gain. #9765. The SageMaker AI Inference Router Moves Requests Across Regions After Errors or Timeouts

Posted on Nov 21 • Originally published at blog.neticslabs.com

Salesforce's Agentforce Foundation team serves models from the Region a request originates in, across more than thirty global Regions and hundreds of AWS accounts. Each customer has its own peak window and those windows overlap, so provisioning for the combined peak costs more than the traffic justifies, and provisioning per Region leaves idle instances in one place while another runs out. That gap between fragmented capacity and availability is the problem AWS is selling the router against.

The AWS Machine Learning blog post of 18 November 2026 describing Salesforce's deployment of cross-Region inference routing. Source: aws.amazon.com/blogs/machine-learning, captured 18 November 2026.

Before the router, Salesforce routed overflow through its own Internal Gateway, with health checks, retries and Region-switching logic that the team built and operated. Two gaps made that path expensive. The gateway had no capacity signal from the local or the remote endpoint, so it could not tell when to move traffic or whether the destination had room. Cross-Region traffic also had to leave the VPC through a NAT gateway and an internet gateway and travel over public networking. In design reviews, Salesforce's team raised a third problem that any failover design inherits: shifting load during an incident can overload the Region that receives it, so the receiving side needs a ceiling.

The router is a regional resource in the customer's account. Applications invoke the router with a routing target name and the same body and content type they already send to InvokeEndpoint. The routing target is a name for one logical model, such as a classifier, and it lists the endpoints and inference components that may serve it by full Amazon Resource Name. One router holds one routing target per model, so a problem with one model's destinations leaves the others alone, and a target can mix single-model endpoints with inference components.

Figure 1 from the AWS post: each Region's Internal Gateway calls the local router through a VPC endpoint, residency-tagged requests stay on the local endpoint, and everything else fails over to an endpoint in another Region. Source: aws.amazon.com/blogs/machine-learning, retrieved 18 November 2026.

Because a destination is identified by ARN, it can live in another account. The owning account attaches a resource-based policy that allows the router account to invoke its endpoint, with a condition that limits access to one named router, so the endpoint owner keeps the revoke switch. This is the piece that makes the pattern usable inside a platform team: the model owner authorises one consumer, and the consumer does not need credentials across the whole account.

The router determines health from recent request outcomes. Platform faults, 5xx responses from the model container, throttles and timeouts lower a destination's standing, and as they persist the router sends a growing share of new requests elsewhere, typically starting within about a minute and taking several minutes for a destination with little traffic. After recovery, traffic returns more slowly than it left, which is what keeps the system from oscillating.

Two exclusions carry most of the design intent. Client errors such as invalid input move nothing, because the same request would fail identically in any Region. Model latency moves nothing either, because a slow answer often reflects a long prompt and says little about endpoint health. The documentation limits the router to one retry on another destination when the destination did not run the model, for example when it throttled the request.

The team ran two configurations. First, same-Region routing inside us-west-2, where the gateway called the local router and the router sent requests to the local endpoint. Then a cross-account, cross-Region setup in which the router in us-west-2 also listed an endpoint in us-east-2 owned by a separate infrastructure account. Before sending production traffic they called DescribeInferenceRouter and confirmed both destinations reported Routable.

The failover test flooded the local endpoint and watched with a separate probe. Probe p50 latency rose from 0.2 seconds to between 45 and 58 seconds across about five minutes of saturation, and traffic stayed in us-west-2 because successful slow responses count as healthy for routing. Once requests exceeded the model container's 60-second handler timeout and started returning errors, the router began to shift. The first requests reached us-east-2 about two minutes after the first errors, and within another minute roughly 78 percent of probe traffic was served there. The remaining 20 to 25 percent stayed local so the router could detect recovery.

Figure 3 from the AWS post: share of probe requests by Region through the failover, with the shift to us-east-2 peaking near 78 percent and a gradual return over about ten minutes. Source: aws.amazon.com/blogs/machine-learning, retrieved 18 November 2026.

The slice that stayed local matters as much as the share that moved. That 20 to 25 percent of probe traffic kept touching the impaired endpoint and supplied the request outcomes the router uses to notice a recovery. Keeping 20 to 25 percent of probe traffic local preserved the request-outcome signal used to detect recovery. The local share follows the router's assessment of destination health.

With traffic moved, p50 latency returned to 0.2 seconds and the cross-Region path added under 100 milliseconds at p50. After the local endpoint recovered, traffic returned to us-west-2 gradually over about ten minutes, and the probe recorded no errors during failover or failback. Salesforce plans to repeat the test with a longer saturation window, measure cross-Region latency at millisecond precision, and inspect cascading behaviour at the traffic cap before widening the rollout.

Netics visual, 18 November 2026: the four numbers that describe the Salesforce failover, including the sub-100-millisecond cross-Region overhead.

Each response carries InvokedRoutedResourceArn and RoutingReason, mirrored in the X-Amzn-SageMaker-Invoked-Routed-Resource-Arn and X-Amzn-SageMaker-Invoked-Routing-Reason headers. The reason takes one of four values: local-preferred for a healthy local destination, failover when a local destination exists and is not serving reliably, capacity-available when no local destination could take the request, and only-healthy when a single eligible destination was the only healthy one. Because the ARN carries Region and account, one log line answers whether a request left its boundary and why.

The aggregate view comes from OpenTelemetry metrics published to CloudWatch in the router's own account and Region: invocations per destination with an error.type attribute splitting 4xx, 5xx including timeouts, and model errors; destination.duration; overhead.duration for the time the router itself adds; and destination.status reporting healthy, overloaded or degraded. Because those metrics sit next to each endpoint's existing SageMaker metrics, teams can query them together in a cross-account dashboard.

Figure 2 from the AWS post: a CloudWatch dashboard during a failover test in which requests per destination shift from the local endpoint and return after recovery. Source: aws.amazon.com/blogs/machine-learning, retrieved 18 November 2026.

Salesforce kept its residency check in the gateway and pinned tagged requests to an in-Region routing target whose only destination is the local endpoint. Those requests never cross a boundary, which is the arrangement a European or public-sector customer will want examined before adoption. Everything else goes to the router with the body, content type and accept type the gateway already sent.

The cap is the second control. CrossRegionTrafficConfig on the receiving endpoint sets a per-instance request rate and the largest share of that endpoint's capacity remote traffic may take, and local traffic never counts against it. When remote traffic reaches the cap, the endpoint stops accepting requests from other Regions and the router looks elsewhere, which is how the design avoids the cascading failure Salesforce's reviewers predicted.

Three obligations survive the managed layer. The same model, container image and artifacts have to exist in every registered Region, because each destination uses the artifacts deployed in its own Region and a destination running a different version answers the same request differently. Each Region has to be sized for its own traffic plus the overflow it expects to absorb, with autoscaling headroom, and its endpoint autoscaling policy supplies additional instances as traffic grows. And the cap has to match a real capacity calculation, since a receiving Region that cannot scale fast enough simply returns its own errors.

Richard Chang, a software engineering architect at Salesforce, frames the outcome in terms of what the team stopped maintaining: "we can add capacity securely and keep our data residency commitments". The engineering reading is narrower and more useful. A routing layer relocates the queue to capacity sized in another Region, and the cap is the part of the design that keeps a bad minute in one Region from becoming a bad hour in two.

Teams that already plan regional capacity for sovereign infrastructure and cloud exit work gain one thing from the router: a model's placement becomes a routing policy with an audit trail, and the questions to answer are which Regions may serve which requests, how much remote traffic each may absorb, and who reads the routing reason when a shift happens.

Netics visual, 18 November 2026: the three obligations a team retains once the router handles health and failover.

#9764. How long can butter sit out?: For the best baking success, here's the deal on saving softened butter for later.

The bakers of King Arthur are here to solve the kitchen conundrums you share with us, whether it’s on the phone, computer, or by the good old postal service. In Ask the Baker’s Hotline, Annabelle will pick the brains of the talented King Arthur Baker’s Hotline team to tackle some of your most-asked questions.

Ryan from our Baker’s Hotline is here with the answer.

You sure can! It will still work the next time you want to bake. But remember, as with any dairy product, there are always precautions to take.

The USDA recommends keeping butter at room temperature for no more than two days to prevent spoilage. Salt is a preservative and can lengthen the shelf life, but for the sake of this article, we’re talking about unsalted butter. (It’s more appropriate for baking and is the type called for in most King Arthur recipes.)

“If the butter has only been on the counter at room temperature for a few hours or overnight and has maintained a temperature below 70°F, it should be just fine to place back in the fridge,” says Ryan. “You may not notice a difference in the performance of the butter when you eventually use it, other than the wrapper being a bit wet or soft. Food safety-wise, it’s still good to use.”

“If the butter became very soft or started to melt during its time on the counter (or in the microwave if you were speeding up the process), you can put it back in the fridge, but it may not be the best to use in your recipe,” Ryan suggests. “You may notice when it solidifies that it’s separated or grainy. The water, fats, and solids in butter are an emulsion, which can break when melted and re-solidified.” If your recipe depends on butter to create air or structure, like a cake that calls for creaming butter and sugar, you’ll want to start over with new butter.

“If you used that butter in a recipe requiring creaming, the air you incorporate wouldn’t be as stable since the structure of the butter has changed,” Ryan says. “Your baked goods may not rise properly, and frostings may be soft and loose. Is it still safe to use? Food safety-wise, yes. But structure-wise, perhaps not.”

That butter can still be used for other things though! Extra-softened or even melted and re-solidified butter will still work perfectly to spread on toast or pancakes, to be made into brown butter, or to remelt and use in recipes calling for melted butter like a Graham Cracker Crust.

If your butter has been unrefrigerated for more than two days, you run the risk of it going rancid. As Ryan says, “There is no coming back from rancid butter.” It has a distinctly unpleasant flavor and a noticeable rancid smell that carries over into baked goods. It’s best to dispose of the butter if this happens.

But what if you want to keep your butter at room temperature for days at a time to slather on your morning toast? Ryan recommends storing your butter in a butter keeper if you want to leave it on the counter. “The water in the base of the jar creates an airtight seal, helping prevent the butter from spoiling. So long as it is stored away from direct heat and light, the butter in a container like this will be fine for a few days. Be sure to replace the water often and clean the container before filling again.”

“When working with butter in a recipe, I like to bring out and soften only the amount that is needed for what I am working on. That way, I don’t end up with extra butter that won’t be used right away,” he says. “Repeatedly moving butter from the fridge to the counter and then back invites spoilage and poor performance.”

In a rush? To soften your butter more quickly, Ryan advises, “Cut your butter into pats and place them on a plate in a single layer at room temperature. More surface area means that the butter will soften a bit faster!”

#9762. Most Frequently Asked Questions About Affiliate Marketing

Affiliate marketing is a way to make money by promoting the products and services of other people and companies. You don't need to create your product or service, just promote existing ones. That's why it's so easy to get started with affiliate marketing. You can even get started with no budget at all!

An affiliate program is a package of information you create for your product, which is then made available to potential publishers. The program will typically include details about the product and its retail value, commission levels, and promotional materials. Many affiliate programs are managed via an affiliate network like ShareASale, which acts as a platform to connect publishers and advertisers, but it is also possible to offer your program directly.

Affiliate networks connect publishers to advertisers.  Affiliate networks make money by charging fees to the merchants who advertise with them; these merchants are known as advertisers. The percentage of each sale that the advertiser pays is negotiated between the merchant and the affiliate network.

Dropshipping is a method of selling that allows you to run an online store without having to stock products. You advertise the products as if you owned them, but when someone makes an order, you create a duplicate order with the distributor at a reduced price. The distributor takes care of the post and packaging on your behalf. As affiliate marketing is based on referrals and this type of drop shipping requires no investment in inventory when a customer buys through the affiliate link, no money exchanges hands.

Performance marketing is a method of marketing that pays for performance, like when a sale is made or an ad is clicked This can include methods like PPC (pay-per-click) or display advertising. Affiliate marketing is one form of performance marketing where commissions are paid out to affiliates on a performance basis when they click on their affiliate link and make a purchase or action.

Smartphones are essentially miniature computers, so publishers can display the same websites and offers that are available on a PC. But mobiles also offer specific tools not available on computers, and these can be used to good effect for publishers. Publishers can optimize their ads for mobile users by making them easy to access by this audience. Publishers can also make good use of text and instant messaging to promote their offers. As the mobile market is predicted to make up 80% of traffic in the future, publishers who do not promote on mobile devices are missing out on a big opportunity.

The best way to find affiliate publishers is on reputable networks like ShareASale Cj(Commission Junction), Awin, and Impact radius. These networks have a strict application process and compliance checks, which means that all affiliates are trustworthy.

An affiliate disclosure statement discloses to the reader that there may be affiliate links on a website, for which a commission may be paid to the publisher if visitors follow these links and make purchases.

Publishers promote their programs through a variety of means, including blogs, websites, email marketing, and pay-per-click ads. Social media has a huge interactive audience, making this platform a good source of potential traffic.

A super affiliate is an affiliate partner who consistently drives a large majority of sales from any program they promote, compared to other affiliate partners involved in that program.  Affiliates make a lot of money from affiliate marketing Pat Flynn earned more than $50000 in 2013 from affiliate marketing.

Because the Internet is so widespread, affiliate programs can be promoted in any country. Affiliate strategies that are set internationally need to be tailored to the language of the targeted country.

Affiliate marketing can help you grow your business in the following ways:

One of the best ways to work with qualified affiliates is to hire an affiliate marketing agency that works with all the networks. Affiliates are carefully selected and go through a rigorous application process to be included in the network.

Affiliate marketing is generally associated with websites, but there are other ways to promote your affiliate links, including:

To build your affiliate marketing business, you don't have to invest money in the beginning. You can sign up for free with any affiliate network and start promoting their brands right away.

Commission rates are typically based on a percentage of the total sale and in some cases can also be a flat fee for each transaction. The rates are set by the merchant.

Some merchants run their affiliate programs internally, while others choose to contract out management to a network or an external agency.

#9760. What is piloncillo? This sweetener makes great cookies, pan dulce, and more: Use this traditional Mexican unrefined sugar for a dash of flavor and history.

This article is part of our feature celebrating Pan Dulce. Find all things pan dulce here.

Categorically, piloncillo is a “non-centrifugal” cane sugar, meaning it is an unrefined sugar product and a true natural brown sugar. It’s mostly consumed in Mexico and Latin America, but a similar product can be found in Asia, known as jaggery in India. Though often lumped together, these unrefined dark sugars are very different from brown sugars on the market today, which have been refined to a large degree — in some cases, they’re actually just white sugar with coloring or molasses added.

Making piloncillo, on the other hand, involves an artisanal process that’s hundreds of years old. To make it, pressed cane juice is boiled to evaporate the water and deeply caramelize the sugar. The cooked cane is then poured into molds (often made of wood) and left to dry and harden. Traditional piloncillo is conical in shape and can vary in size from small to large cones but is most commonly found in a medium size that weighs about 200 grams. In Guatemala and Colombia, it is called panela, where it is cooked to a lighter degree and typically formed into a brick, rather than cone, shape. Other forms of piloncillo can be granulated or liquid (which is more rare).

Minimally processed and boldly flavored, piloncillo was historically a prized and respected foodstuff. As an unrefined cane sugar, piloncillo provides more complex vitamins and minerals than refined sugars, which undergo processing and whitening methods that also strip nutrients from the whole food. And piloncillo is also great for baking, providing notes of burnt caramel and hints of smoke. Plus, its rich molasses qualities keep baked goods moist and fresh for longer.

Always look at the ingredient label when purchasing piloncillo and make sure it says 100% pure cane juice or cane sugar. It is becoming increasingly common to find imitation products marketed as jaggery or piloncillo that contain coloring and corn syrup. You can find good piloncillo at specialty grocery stores or online at retailers.

In Mexico and throughout Latin America, piloncillo is an important ingredient in many traditional dishes. (Some will even say it’s not the “real dish” if you substitute sugar in these recipes due to the deep flavors and richness that only piloncillo can provide.) This deep, dark unrefined sugar lends its characteristic flavor and texture to popular foods and beverages such as capirotada, tepache, coyotas, atole, café de olla, calabaza al horno, coricos, and hojarascas, to name a few!

I love adding piloncillo when I’m making champurrado. In this warm and thick chocolate beverage, the piloncillo is chopped or grated and dissolved in the pot with water or milk before adding the chocolate and masa. In this recipe, the piloncillo’s intense sweet and smoky flavors pair well with the chocolate and corn masa.

While there are many dishes and uses for piloncillo, it’s not a simple substitution for granulated white sugar in recipes, but you can use it the same as you would brown sugar with a 1:1 substitution by weight.  Depending on how hard the cone is, it can be crumbled or grated for easier measuring. If it is very hard, try cutting it in half with a sharp knife and then placing it between parchment paper or a towel and beating with a rolling pin.

Then, Acrolinx checks and scores your existing content to find what’s working and suggest areas for improvement. #9756. Add This Creamy Dip To Ground Beef For Juicier, More Flavorful Burgers

We may receive a commission on purchases made from links.

The perfect burger can be hard to come by. When you're going out, Food Republic's list of the best burgers in every state can be helpful, and there are even some great fast food options. But when you're looking for a super juicy and flavorful homemade grilled or pan-fried patty, what's the best route to take?

Sometimes, it all comes down to what you mix into the ground beef. While Bobby Flay uses only salt and pepper to season his patties, some folks swear by Worcestershire sauce and garlic powder for a kick of flavor. But there's one ingredient you may not have thought of that will keep your end result wonderfully succulent. Try mixing some onion dip into your ground beef. It's one of the clever ingredients that make burgers juicier, and it will add loads of flavor.

Onion dips generally come seasoned with dried onion and garlic, salt, and other herbs, plus a little sugar for sweetness. Add to that the sour cream base, and you have a rich, bold, slightly tangy, umami-filled burst of flavor that won't overpower your taste buds. And because you're mixing the dip directly into the beef before cooking, it can help keep your patties nice and moist (as long as you don't overcook them). Sour cream is simply cultured cream, so it has a high moisture content, and the added seasonings aren't so coarse that they will burn before the beef itself is cooked.

When it comes to what dip to use, classics like Dean's French Onion or Daisy Sour Cream French Onion, which is available on Amazon, will work great, but pretty much any brand will work. Depending on how much tangy flavor you want, you'll need about a half-cup to a full cup of dip per 2 pounds of beef.

The beauty of using onion dip in your burgers is that it's a one-ingredient solution, but you can increase the intensity with extra onion powder or fresh minced or dried onions. Just don't overdo it on the onion pieces, or the patties could fall apart on the grill. If you're going heavy on the amount of dip you use, you may want to think about adding some breadcrumbs as a binding agent. Dried parsley makes a great mix-in, as do other Italian herbs, but you should start sparingly so they don't overpower the flavor you're aiming for.

As for toppings, the regular stuff will do, but you might want to hold off on the ketchup and mustard until you've had a bite. Caramelized onions are an obvious choice, or you can give your burger some crunch with crispy fried onions. And you can always add an extra dollop of onion dip on top for more creamy flavor and texture.

Lastly, this trick will also work with a dried dip mix. Just mix it in with sour cream before you make the burgers. And if you want a similarly juicy bite without the added zing, try using mayonnaise in your burger. But for a juicy texture and plenty of zesty flavor, grab that onion dip out of the fridge.
